diagnostic_evidence.quote: To ensure the injectivity of the encoder approximated by a neural network, each layer must be injective, condition which is satisfied when $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ for all hidden layers, so $n_\ell \geq n_\text{in}$ for $\ell = 1,\ldots,L-1$.
By \Cref{th:uap}, we have that $n_\ell = n_\text{in}+n_\text{out}$ is sufficient to satisfy $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ and $\lim_{|\myw|\to\infty}\Varepsilon_2 = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's inference is false: a layer with $n_\ell \geq n_{\ell-1}$ need not be injective. E.g., the ReLU layer $\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2$, $x\mapsto(\max(x_1,0),\max(x_2,0))$, has equal widths but collapses the whole negative quadrant to $0$; any affine map with a nontrivial kernel is non-injective regardless of width, and even full-rank affine maps followed by ReLU are non-injective. Hence the stated width condition is not a sufficient condition for injectivity of the encoder (on $\mathbb{R}^N$ or, in general, on $\mathcal{M}$). Additionally, the appeal to the universal approximation theorem (th:uap) only yields $\varepsilon$-approximation, not the exact identity $\Varepsilon_1 = 0$ claimed in the proof.

failure_location.quote: A sufficient condition for the width to ensure injectivity of the encoder is $n_\ell \geq n_	ext{in}$, for $\ell = 1,\ldots, L-1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem with explicit layer-wise injectivity hypotheses (e.g., strictly monotone activations such as ELU/PReLU and full-column-rank affine maps for $\ell=1,\ldots,L-1$, plus injectivity of the final linear map on the reshaped manifold $\psi'(\mathcal{M})$); under those added hypotheses the conclusion holds, so the design message is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The architecture-design guideline that the dimension reduction must be performed only at the last layer loses its formal justification; the main-results bullet in the introduction and the remark restating the message of th:reduction are unsupported as formal claims (the qualitative guidance survives only heuristically).
issues.title: Th:reduction — non-decreasing layer widths do not ensure encoder injectivity
issues.why_classification: The stated sufficient condition is false and must be withdrawn or replaced, but a contained strengthening of hypotheses repairs the theorem without changing the qualitative architecture guidance; no new global proof architecture is needed and no rate or regime is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimate for $\overline{L}_{F_n,\mu}$ uses the Lipschitz constant $L_{F_N}$ of $F_N$, but the proposition's hypotheses assume only that $\Psi,\Psi'$ are Lipschitz and that $F_N$ is bounded; well-posedness of the N-ODE (existence/uniqueness/continuous dependence) does not imply Lipschitz continuity of $F_N$. The bound is therefore unproven under the stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Additionally, we assume that $F_N$ is bounded, with $M_{F_N} \coloneqq \sup_{u_N\in\mathcal{M}} \|F_N(u_N)\|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $F_N$ is Lipschitz continuous with constant $L_{F_N}$ to the statement of th:L_{F_n}; the estimate in the proposition and appendix and all downstream uses then go through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: th:well_posedness_node, whose proof cites th:L_{F_n}, inherits the gap; the same missing hypothesis propagates to every bound built on $L_{F_n}$ (the Lyapunov bounds eq:lyapunov_stab_node/eq:lyapunov_stab_Node, the B-stability timestep bound eq:b_stab_timestep_bound, and the exponential factor in th:global_convergence).
issues.title: Th:L_{F_n} — Lipschitz continuity of F_N is used but never assumed
issues.why_classification: A standard local condition repairs the defect; every substantive claim, guarantee, and rate survives, so the issue is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We now assume the construction of an autoencoder that realizes an orthogonal projection.

issues.failure_explanation: With $P = J_\Psi J_{\Psi'}$ an orthogonal projection onto an $n$-dimensional subspace $S$, the nonzero eigenvalues of $A = J_{\Psi'}\Lambda J_\Psi$ are the eigenvalues of the compression $P\Lambda|_S$, which in general are not eigenvalues of $\Lambda$. Counterexample: $\Lambda = \mathrm{diag}(-3,-5)$ and $S = \mathrm{span}\{(1,1)\}$ (e.g., $J_{\Psi'} = [1\ 1]$, $J_\Psi = [1;1]/2$) gives the single compression eigenvalue $-4 \notin \{-3,-5\}$; the node's Forward Euler stability limit is then $2/4 = 0.5$, strictly smaller than the N-ODE limit $2/3$, contradicting the claim that the timestep bound is, even in the worst scenario, the same.

failure_location.quote: Due to the specific assumptions made in the construction of the decoder, the projection sets some eigenvalues to zero while leaving the others unchanged. Therefore, the eigenvalues $\neq 0$ are those of $\Lambda$, so the bound on the timestep of the node is, in the worst scenario, the same as that of the \Node.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claim by the correct spectral statement: the FE timestep bound for the node is governed by the eigenvalues of $P\Lambda|_S$, which must be computed or bounded separately; the sentence asserting that the nonzero eigenvalues are those of $\Lambda$ must be withdrawn.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised 'no worse than the N-ODE' timestep guarantee for the reduced scheme is false; the correct statement must be phrased in terms of the compression spectrum (for symmetric $\Lambda$, Cauchy interlacing relates it to the spectrum of $\Lambda$ but does not make it coincide). The surrounding conclusions — that the stability bound must be checked for the specific autoencoder — remain valid.
issues.title: A-stability: nonzero eigenvalues of the reduced FE matrix are not those of Lambda
issues.why_classification: A materially false guarantee must be withdrawn and the spectral analysis reworked (a contained but nontrivial correction, e.g., via interlacing bounds); the advertised 'same bound' property is lost, though the rest of the section survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, setting \eqref{eq:what_nn_learns_1} to zero and comparing it to \eqref{eq:diff_op_tau}, we conclude that
A necessary condition to meet the requirement $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$ is that $\tau_n^k, \zeta_k \to 0$ and $\kappa \to 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: Setting the residual loss \eqref{eq:loss_2_fully_datadriven} to zero and comparing with the truncation-error identity \eqref{eq:diff_op_tau} only controls the multistep combination $\sum_p \beta_p (N_{F_n} - F_n)$ evaluated at training states, not the pointwise maximum over all $k$; for $P \geq 2$ pointwise convergence does not follow even on training data. Moreover, subtracting the two identities shows the encoder error enters as $\Delta t_\text{train}^{-1} \sum_p \alpha_p \kappa$, so the stated necessary condition $\kappa \to 0$ does not make that term vanish — one needs $\kappa = o(\Delta t_\text{train})$. The stated convergence claim and the stated necessary condition are both unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: The fully data-driven is a convergent method for training $N_{F_n}$ in the sense that, under proper conditions, $\max_{k=0,1,\ldots}\|N_{F_n}(t_k) - F_n(t_k)\| \to 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim (e.g., to one-step schemes with dense training data and $\kappa = o(\Delta t_\text{train})$, concluding convergence on training states) or supply a genuine argument controlling $N_{F_n} - F_n$ pointwise; correct the necessary condition to $\kappa = o(\Delta t_\text{train})$.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence claim for fully data-driven training of $N_{F_n}$ is unsupported; the final limit claim of th:global_convergence explicitly invokes th:fully_works for $\eps_{F_n} \to 0$ and is affected for the fully data-driven strategy (the error bound of th:global_convergence itself remains valid).
issues.title: Th:fully_works — zero residual loss does not yield pointwise convergence of N_{F_n} to F_n
issues.why_classification: A necessary nontrivial argument is missing and the stated guarantee does not follow, but a contained repair (restricted claim plus a corrected necessary condition) leaves a recognizably comparable result; no global proof architecture is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and the following vector whose elements are the solution at each timesteps: $\m \uut_n = [\uut_n^0, \uut_n^1, \ldots, \uut_n^K]^T$

with the following auxiliary conditions for the first $P-1$ steps, derived from a one-sided finite difference of the same order of convergence of the $P$-steps scheme: \begin{equation}\label{eq:auxiliary_conditions} \sum_{p=0}^{P}\gamma_p\uut_n^{k+p}=\Delta t N_{F_n}(\uut_n^k), \quad k=0,\ldots,P-1. \end{equation}

issues.failure_explanation: The stacked system has $(K-P+1) + (P-1) = K$ equations for the $K+1$ unknowns of $\m \uut_n$, and no initial-condition row appears even though the surrounding text says the matrix form has 'initial conditions included'. The declared dimensions ($K$ columns) are incompatible with $\m \uut_n \in \mathbb{R}^{K+1}$; the displayed row pattern of $\Gamma$ places $\gamma_P$ in the last column, matching auxiliary index $k = K-P$ rather than the stated range $k = 0,\ldots,P-1$ (consistent only when $K = 2P-1$, while the text assumes $K \geq 2P-1$); and '$P-1$ steps' contradicts the displayed range $k=0,\ldots,P-1$, which is $P$ values. As written the system does not determine the discrete solution.

failure_location.quote: The solution in time of the \node\ is obtained from the following non-linear system:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $A, B, \Gamma, C$ with $K+1$ columns and row patterns matching the stated equation ranges, reconcile the auxiliary-condition count ($k=0,\ldots,P-2$ for $P-1$ equations), and add the initial-condition row $\uut_n^0 = N_{\Psi'}(u_N^0)$; the construction then determines the solution as claimed.
issues.overall_effect: The matrix formulation of the fully discrete problem is unusable as stated; th:global_convergence references this matrix form, and any reader implementing the assembled system obtains an underdetermined problem.
issues.title: Eq:sys_lmm — assembled discrete system is underdetermined and mis-dimensioned
issues.why_classification: The repair is routine linear-algebra bookkeeping (dimension and index corrections plus one initial-condition row); the construction's purpose and all subsequent claims survive, so the issue is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We observe a consistent overestimation of the total concentration.

issues.failure_explanation: The added term is the componentwise reconstruction error, i.e., the same quantity already minimized by the autoencoder loss $\mathscr{N}_{ij}^1$; it constrains $N_\Psi$ only at training snapshots and imposes no constraint on the invariant $\sum_k [N_\Psi(\uut_n)]_k = \mathrm{const}$ along trajectories generated by $N_{F_n}$. Hence its minimization does not enforce conservation, contrary to the prose claim; the small observed conservation error is attributable to reconstruction accuracy, not to the claimed mechanism.

failure_location.quote: To this aim, a simple strategy is to modify the loss function by adding a contribution whose minimization enforces conservation: \begin{equation*} \mathscr{N}_{ij}^\text{cons} = \sum_{k=1}^{N=19} \|[u_{N,i}^j]_k - [N_{\Psi}(\uut_{n,i}^j)]_k\|_2^2. \end{equation*}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term with a penalty that targets the invariant directly, e.g., $\big|\sum_k [N_\Psi(\uut_{n,i}^j)]_k - \sum_k [u_{N,i}^j]_k\big|^2$ or deviation of the reconstructed total mass from its initial value; a contained change to the training objective.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed structure-preservation mechanism in Test 3 is misdescribed; the claim that the modification enforces conservation of the total concentration is unsupported.
issues.title: Chemistry test: the added 'conservation' loss does not enforce the total-concentration invariant
issues.why_classification: The construction is a heuristic in a numerical experiment and the observed conservation is already good; the fix is a short local modification of the loss, so the issue is minor.
